data.title: RGA Uses Heavy Vehicle Simulator to Test Road Durability over 20 Years
data.content:
Riyadh, November 22, 2026, SPA -- The Roads General Authority (RGA) has highlighted the capabilities of its Heavy Vehicle Simulator (HVS), an advanced research tool at its road laboratory that replicates real-world operating conditions to assess durability over a 20-year service life.
    The simulator builds a sample of a planned road and subjects it to traffic loads, climatic and geological conditions, and material properties in a controlled laboratory setting. This enables researchers to gauge the wear and tear the section would experience over two decades of actual use.
    The authority explained that the technology accelerates testing and helps predict road performance before construction begins, contributing to more efficient spending, environmental and financial sustainability, and improved lifecycle management of infrastructure projects.
    It noted that the device is the first of its kind in the Gulf region and the Middle East. It features an automated loading mechanism capable of performing 26,000 cycles in both directions within 24 hours, with computer-controlled adjustable limits, and operates at temperatures from 15°C to 60°C.
    The HVS is equipped with automated monitoring and measurement systems, including precision sensors that track temperature, pressure, stress, strain, and other key parameters. These systems continuously record changes in the layers of the section under test and transmit data to a control unit for analysis by a specialized technical team, which provides recommendations accordingly.
    The technology also allows a wide range of scenarios to be tested, covering traffic volumes, climate such as dry and rainy weather, and construction materials used in different environments, including sabkha (salt-flat) areas. This helps ensure road quality under diverse conditions and speeds up the assessment of material and design performance.
    The RGA aims to advance the objectives of the road sector program, which focuses on enhancing safety and quality and easing traffic congestion. It seeks to raise the Kingdom's road quality index to sixth place globally and reduce the fatality rate to fewer than five per 100,000 people by 2030.
    -- SPA
